The permutation test compares real and shuffled estimators to detect redundancy in non-strength features. If ARM B performs significantly worse, it implies these features carry real information; otherwise, they are duplicates. The debiased ECE gate measures calibration error, revealing that even a conservative forecast may fail the 0.06 threshold. Thus, the system's logic chain is: (1) scalarizer detects dominance, (2) permutation reveals redundancy, (3) ECE gate validates calibration. These three operators form a dual failure mode: either a feature is redundant (scalarizer + permutation), or it fails calibration (ECE gate).
